---
title: "Business Forecasting — Assignment #3: ARIMA"
subtitle: |
  SunBridge Solar Installations: When Regression Isn't Enough
  *Can ARIMA Outperform a Trend-Season Regression?*
author: "LastName, FirstName | Student ID: XXXXXXX"



# ── Core forecasting ecosystem ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# fpp3 bundles: tsibble, feasts, fable, lubridate, and tidyverse helpers
library(fpp3)

## Section 1 — Load Data and Create a tsibble

# The CSV uses "Mon-YY" date strings (e.g. "Jan-15").
# lubridate::my() parses this format; yearmonth() converts it to a
# tsibble-compatible monthly period index for time series operations.

sunbridge <- read.csv("SunBridge_Installations.csv") |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(my(Month))) |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month)

glimpse(sunbridge)
summary(sunbridge$Installations)



# Exploratory Data Analysis

## Section 2 — Time Plot, Seasonal Plot, and ACF

# ── Time plot ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
autoplot(sunbridge, Installations) +
  labs(
    title    = "SunBridge Solar: Monthly Installations (Jan 2015 to Dec 2024)",
    subtitle = "Steady upward trend with pronounced summer seasonality",
    y        = "Installations (units)",
    x        = "Month"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1a3a5c"))



# ── Seasonal plot: converted to tibble for clean ggplot control ───────────────
# gg_season() inline labels overlap with 10 years; ggplot with a legend
# is clearer and more professional for publication.

sunbridge |>
  mutate(
    Year = factor(year(Month)),
    Mon  = month(Month, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)
  ) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Mon, y = Installations, colour = Year, group = Year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "turbo") +
  labs(
    title  = "Seasonal Plot: SunBridge Installations by Month",
    x      = "Month",
    y      = "Installations (units)",
    colour = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# ── ACF of raw series (up to 36 lags = 3 seasonal cycles) ────────────────────
sunbridge |>
  ACF(Installations, lag_max = 36) |>
  autoplot() +
  labs(
    title    = "ACF of Raw Monthly Installations",
    subtitle = "Slow decay + 12-period scallops = trend AND seasonality",
    y        = "Autocorrelation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1a3a5c"))


# Model Progression

## Section 3 — Data Partitioning


# ── Temporal train / validation split ────────────────────────────────────────
# Training   (Jan 2015 - Dec 2022): 96 months = 8 complete calendar years
# Validation (Jan 2023 - Dec 2024): 24 months = 2 complete calendar years
#
# A strict out-of-time holdout simulates real deployment: the model never
# observes validation data during fitting. Two full validation years capture
# two complete seasonal cycles for a robust out-of-sample accuracy estimate.

train <- sunbridge |> filter(year(Month) <= 2022)   # 96 months
valid <- sunbridge |> filter(year(Month) >= 2023)   # 24 months

cat("Training set  :", nrow(train), "months — Jan 2015 to Dec 2022\n")
cat("Validation set:", nrow(valid), "months — Jan 2023 to Dec 2024\n")


## Section 4 — TSLM: Trend + Season Baseline


# ── Fit TSLM ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# TSLM regresses Installations on:
#   trend()   -> deterministic linear time index        (1 coefficient)
#   season()  -> 11 monthly dummy variables             (11 coefficients)
#                (January is the implicit baseline month)
# Total: 1 intercept + 1 trend + 11 dummies = 13 estimated parameters

fit_tslm <- train |>
  model(TrendSeason = TSLM(Installations ~ trend() + season()))

report(fit_tslm)



# ── Forecast over the 24-month validation window ──────────────────────────────
fc_tslm <- fit_tslm |> forecast(new_data = valid)

fc_tslm |>
  autoplot(sunbridge, level = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = "TSLM Forecast: Trend + Season Model",
    subtitle = "Validation period: Jan 2023 to Dec 2024",
    y        = "Installations (units)",
    x        = "Month"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1a3a5c"))

# ── Validation accuracy on the held-out 24 months ────────────────────────────
accuracy(fc_tslm, sunbridge) |>
  select(.model, ME, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, MASE)

## Section 5 — TSLM Residual Diagnostics


# ── Three-panel residual diagnostic ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Panel 1: Time plot of residuals — should be random scatter around zero
# Panel 2: ACF of residuals    — bars should stay within the 95% blue bands
# Panel 3: Histogram           — should be bell-shaped and centred at zero

fit_tslm |>
  gg_tsresiduals() +
  ggtitle("TSLM Residual Diagnostics: Trend + Season Model")



# ── Ljung-Box portmanteau test ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# H0: residuals are white noise (no autocorrelation through lag 24)
# H1: at least one autocorrelation through lag 24 is non-zero
# lag = 24 is standard for monthly data (two full seasonal cycles)

augment(fit_tslm) |>
  features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 24)

## Section 6 — Fit an Automatic ARIMA Model


# ── Step A: Fit automatic ARIMA ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# ARIMA() in fable uses a stepwise AICc search over (p,d,q)(P,D,Q)[12]:
#   Step 1: KPSS/ADF unit-root tests determine d and D automatically.
#   Step 2: Stepwise grid search over p, q, P, Q minimises AICc.
#   Step 3: The winning specification is re-estimated by Maximum Likelihood.

fit_arima <- train |>
  model(ARIMA_auto = ARIMA(Installations))

# ── Step B: View selected order and estimated coefficients ────────────────────
# Selected model: ARIMA(2,0,0)(2,1,0)[12] w/ drift

report(fit_arima)




## Section 7 — ARIMA Residual Diagnostics


# ── Step C: Three-panel residual diagnostic for ARIMA ────────────────────────
# Note: ggtitle updated to reflect the correct model selected by R
fit_arima |>
  gg_tsresiduals() +
  ggtitle("ARIMA Residual Diagnostics: ARIMA(2,0,0)(2,1,0)[12] w/ drift")


# ── Step D: Ljung-Box test on ARIMA residuals ─────────────────────────────────
# Using lag = 24 for consistency with the TSLM test in Section 5
# Target: p > 0.05 (fail to reject H0 -> residuals are white noise)

augment(fit_arima) |>
  features(.innov, ljung_box, lag = 24)
# Actual output: lb_stat = 20.98, lb_pvalue = 0.6399


# Comparison and Deployment Decision

## Section 8 — Fit Both Models Together

# ── Step E: Fit TSLM and ARIMA together in a single mable ─────────────────────
# Fitting both in one call ensures identical training data and a consistent
# evaluation framework; accuracy() and glance() operate uniformly across both.

fit_both <- train |>
  model(
    TrendSeason = TSLM(Installations ~ trend() + season()),
    ARIMA_auto  = ARIMA(Installations)
  )

# ── Step F: Forecast both models and compute validation accuracy ───────────────
fc_both <- fit_both |> forecast(new_data = valid)

accuracy(fc_both, sunbridge) |>
  select(.model, ME, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, MASE) |>
  arrange(MASE)

# ── Step G: Overlay forecast plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────
fc_both |>
  autoplot(sunbridge, level = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = "TSLM vs ARIMA: Forecast Comparison (Validation 2023-2024)",
    subtitle = "Black = actuals  |  Blue = TSLM  |  Orange = ARIMA",
    y        = "Installations (units)",
    x        = "Month"
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Model")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1a3a5c"))

# ── Step H: AICc comparison on the training set ───────────────────────────────
# AICc measures in-sample model quality, penalised for complexity.
# Lower AICc = better balance between fit and parsimony on training data.
# Note: AICc winner on training data does not guarantee best out-of-sample
# forecast accuracy — validation accuracy is the operationally relevant measure.

glance(fit_both) |>
  select(.model, AICc) |>
  arrange(AICc)
